meta.note_zh: 条目为项目自撰摘要，不是原文翻译；标题保留原题，来源与日期以 DOI 记录为准，点击可跳转期刊页核验。
meta.note_en: Entries are project-written summaries, not translations. Original titles are kept; source and date follow the DOI record and link to the journal page for verification.

items.title_zh: 流式脑到语音接口：让合成语音带上自然语调
items.title_en: A streaming brain-to-voice neuroprosthesis to restore naturalistic communication
items.summary_zh: 研究团队用皮层脑电实时解码参与者「尝试说话」的过程，边解码边合成语音，而不是等整句说完再生成。合成语音保留了语调与节奏，延迟接近自然对话，目标是让严重瘫痪者恢复可听懂、可打断的交流。限制在于被试数量少、需要长期植入与个体化校准。
items.summary_en: Cortical activity was decoded in a streaming fashion while a participant attempted to speak, synthesizing speech on the fly rather than after a full sentence. The output preserved intonation and rhythm at near-conversational latency, aiming at intelligible, interruptible communication for people with severe paralysis. Limits: very few participants and a need for long-term implants and individual calibration.

items.title_zh: 快速校准的语音神经假体
items.title_en: An Accurate and Rapidly Calibrating Speech Neuroprosthesis
items.summary_zh: 针对肌萎缩侧索硬化（ALS）患者，研究把皮层内微电极阵列记录的神经活动解码为尝试说出的词句。工作重点是缩短校准时间：不需要漫长的个体化训练就能达到较高准确率，让设备更快可用。限制是单中心小样本，植入电极的长期稳定性仍待随访。
items.summary_en: In a person with ALS, intracortical microelectrode recordings were decoded into attempted words and sentences. The emphasis was calibration speed: usable accuracy without prolonged individual training. Limits: a single-center, very small sample, with long-term electrode stability still under follow-up.

items.title_zh: 用非侵入脑记录解码听到的语音
items.title_en: Decoding speech perception from non-invasive brain recordings
items.summary_zh: 研究用 MEG/EEG 记录参与者听语音时的脑活动，借助自监督语音模型把脑信号与语音表征对齐，从而识别被试听到的内容。相比线性基线，方法在跨被试场景下更稳。需要区分的是：它解码的是「听到的语音」，不等于自由想象或内语；且依赖大量记录数据。
items.summary_en: MEG/EEG was recorded while participants listened to speech, and a self-supervised speech model aligned brain signals with speech representations to identify what was heard. The approach generalized better than linear baselines across participants. Note the scope: it decodes perceived speech, not free imagery or inner speech, and needs large recording sets.

items.title_zh: 语音解码 + 虚拟形象控制
items.title_en: A high-performance neuroprosthesis for speech decoding and avatar control
items.summary_zh: 研究用皮层脑电同时解码尝试说出的语音与面部动作，驱动一个会说话、有表情的虚拟形象。意义在于把「说出内容」扩展到「怎么说」——语速、韵律与面部表情共同构成可交流的信号。限制是需要开颅植入，且模型要针对个体训练。
items.summary_en: Cortical recordings were decoded into both attempted speech and facial movement, driving a speaking avatar with expressions. The contribution extends communication from what is said to how it is said—rate, prosody and face together. Limits: craniotomy-based implantation and participant-specific model training.

items.summary_zh: 研究在皮层内阵列记录的基础上，用语言模型约束解码输出，把尝试说话转成文本，速度接近自然对话。语言模型的加入显著降低了字符级错误，说明「神经解码 + 语言先验」是当前语音 BCI 的主流组合。限制同样是小样本与植入长期稳定性。
items.summary_en: Intracortical recordings were combined with a language model to turn attempted speech into text at rates approaching natural conversation. The language prior cut character-level errors, making neural decoding plus linguistic prior the current mainstream recipe. Limits remain small samples and long-term implant stability.

items.title_zh: 脑—脊接口让脊髓损伤者自然行走
items.title_en: Walking naturally after spinal cord injury using a brain–spine interface
items.summary_zh: 研究绕过损伤节段：用皮层脑电解码下肢运动意图，实时驱动硬膜外脊髓电刺激，激活损伤以下的运动回路。参与者在辅助下实现站立与行走，步态比单纯持续刺激更自然。限制是单被试、需要外部供电与反复校准，长期安全性待评估。
items.summary_en: The injured segment was bypassed: cortical activity decoded lower-limb intent and drove epidural spinal stimulation in real time, engaging motor circuits below the lesion. A participant achieved standing and walking with support, with more natural gait than continuous stimulation alone. Limits: a single participant, external power and repeated calibration, with long-term safety pending.

items.title_zh: 从非侵入脑记录重建连续语言语义
items.title_en: Semantic reconstruction of continuous language from non-invasive brain recordings
items.summary_zh: 研究用 fMRI 记录听故事或想象故事时的脑活动，结合语言模型解码连续语义，生成的文本能抓住原意而非逐字复现。它证明语义层面的解码不一定要植入电极。限制是 fMRI 体积大、时间分辨率低，需要长时间扫描与被试配合，离实时交流还有距离。
items.summary_en: fMRI during listening to or imagining stories was combined with a language model to decode continuous meaning; the generated text captured gist rather than verbatim words. This shows semantic decoding does not strictly require implants. Limits: fMRI is bulky and slow, needing long scans and participant cooperation—far from real-time conversation.

items.title_zh: 跨物种运动皮层细胞类型比较
items.title_en: Comparative cellular analysis of motor cortex in human, marmoset and mouse
items.summary_zh: 作为 BICCN 计划的一部分，研究用单细胞转录组等技术比较人、狨猴与小鼠运动皮层的细胞类型，发现人类特有的细胞类型与比例差异。它为「人类皮层为何不同」提供了细胞层面的参照，也为后续把动物结果外推到人提供了边界。限制是图谱多为群体平均，功能验证仍需电生理与行为实验补齐。
items.summary_en: Part of the BICCN effort, this work compared cell types in human, marmoset and mouse motor cortex using single-cell transcriptomics and related methods, revealing human-specific types and proportions. It gives a cellular reference for why human cortex differs and bounds how animal findings extrapolate. Limits: atlases are population averages, with functional validation still needed.

items.title_zh: 哺乳动物初级运动皮层多模态细胞图谱
items.title_en: A multimodal cell census and atlas of the mammalian primary motor cortex
items.summary_zh: 研究整合转录组、表观遗传、形态与电生理多模态数据，给出初级运动皮层的细胞普查与图谱，并建立跨模态对齐框架。它的价值不只是「列清单」，而是让不同实验室的数据能放在同一坐标系里比较。限制是数据整合与功能注释仍在持续修订。
items.summary_en: Transcriptomic, epigenetic, morphological and electrophysiological data were integrated into a cell census and atlas of primary motor cortex, with a cross-modal alignment framework. Its value is not just a list but a shared coordinate system for comparing data across labs. Limits: integration and functional annotation are still being revised.

items.title_zh: 用「想象手写」实现高性能脑到文本
items.summary_zh: 研究让参与者想象手写字母，解码皮层内阵列记录的神经活动并转成文本。相比逐字母点选，利用手写的连续运动表征显著提高了输入速度，是脑到文本路线的重要转折。限制是需要植入阵列与个体化训练，字母集与语言范围也有限。
items.summary_en: A participant imagined handwriting letters while intracortical activity was decoded into text. Exploiting the continuous motor representation of handwriting raised throughput well above letter-by-letter selection—an important turn for brain-to-text. Limits: implanted arrays, individual training and a constrained alphabet and language scope.

items.title_zh: 经血管植入的支架电极：不开颅的神经接口
items.title_en: Motor neuroprosthesis implanted with neurointerventional surgery improves capacity for activities of daily living tasks in severe paralysis
items.summary_zh: 研究通过静脉把支架式电极送入颅内血管壁，避免开颅，记录邻近皮层的场电位。两名 ALS 参与者用思考试用数字界面完成点击、打字等日常任务。它的意义是把植入风险显著降低；限制是通道数与带宽有限，长期血管内稳定性仍需观察。
items.summary_en: A stent-mounted electrode was delivered through a vein to the wall of an intracranial vessel, avoiding craniotomy, and recorded nearby cortical field potentials. Two participants with ALS used thought to operate a digital interface for clicking and typing. The gain is much lower implantation risk; limits are channel count, bandwidth and long-term intravascular stability.

items.title_zh: 从神经活动解码语句并合成语音
items.title_en: Speech synthesis from neural decoding of spoken sentences
items.summary_zh: 研究用皮层脑电解码发声器官的运动学表征，再驱动语音合成器生成可听懂的句子。关键思路是先解码「怎么说」（构音运动），再合成声音，而不是直接拼词。它奠定了后续语音 BCI 的两级路线。限制是需开颅记录、模型离线运行且依赖个体数据。
items.summary_en: Cortical activity was decoded into articulatory kinematics and then drove a synthesizer to produce intelligible sentences. The key idea is decoding how speech is produced before synthesizing sound, rather than assembling words directly—a two-stage blueprint for later speech BCIs. Limits: craniotomy, offline models and participant-specific data.

items.title_zh: 四肢瘫痪者用神经信号控制机械臂抓取
items.title_en: Reach and grasp by people with tetraplegia using a neurally controlled robotic arm
items.summary_zh: 两名四肢瘫痪参与者通过皮层内微电极阵列的神经信号控制机械臂，完成伸手、抓取与把杯子送到嘴边。它是「侵入式 BCI 能恢复复杂日常动作」的早期硬证据，也暴露了当时的局限：有线连接、实验室环境、自由度与稳定性有限。
items.summary_en: Two participants with tetraplegia used intracortical array signals to control a robotic arm for reaching, grasping and bringing a cup to the mouth. It was early hard evidence that invasive BCI can restore complex daily actions, while exposing limits of the time: tethered connections, lab settings, limited degrees of freedom and stability.
